endpoints.summary: Audio Isolation - Extract sounds from audio/video
endpoints.description:
Isolate and extract specific sounds from audio or video files using SAM Audio AI technology.
Describe the sound you want to isolate, and the API separates it from background noise.

**Use cases:**
- Extract speech from noisy recordings
- Isolate musical instruments from a mix
- Separate specific sound effects from video audio
- Remove background noise while preserving target sounds

**Input options:**
- Provide either an `audio` URL/base64 or a `video` URL/base64 (mutually exclusive)
- Supported audio formats: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A
- Supported video formats: MP4, MOV, WEBM, AVI
- For video input, use bounding box coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2) to focus on a specific region

**Output:** WAV audio file containing the isolated sound

description.description: Text description of the sound to isolate from the input audio or video. Be specific about the type of sound you want to extract.

audio.description: Audio input - either a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or base64 encoded audio. Supported formats: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A. Mutually exclusive with `video`.

video.description: Video input - either a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or base64 encoded video. Supported formats: MP4, MOV, WEBM, AVI. Mutually exclusive with `audio`.

x1.description: Bounding box x1 coordinate (left edge) in pixels for sound source localization. Only applicable for video input.

y1.description: Bounding box y1 coordinate (top edge) in pixels for sound source localization. Only applicable for video input.

x2.description: Bounding box x2 coordinate (right edge) in pixels for sound source localization. Only applicable for video input.

y2.description: Bounding box y2 coordinate (bottom edge) in pixels for sound source localization. Only applicable for video input.

sample_fps.description: Frame sampling rate in FPS for video processing. Higher values provide more temporal precision but increase processing time.

reranking_candidates.description: Number of reranking candidates for quality vs latency trade-off. Higher values produce better quality but slower processing.

predict_spans.description: Enable span prediction for better isolation of non-ambient sounds like speech or musical notes.

endpoints.summary: Flows - Run a flow
endpoints.description:
Triggers the execution of a flow. Provide values for all required inputs
defined in the flow's definition (see the GET endpoint).

The `inputs` object maps each input's `api_key` (recommended) or its `id` (UUID, legacy) to its value:

| Input Type | Accepted Values |
|------------|----------------|
| `creation` | Image URL (`https://...`), base64-encoded image string, or existing creation identifier |
| `text` | Plain text string |
| `number` | Numeric value |
| `select` | Value from allowed options |

**This endpoint is asynchronous.** It returns immediately with `status: "running"` and a
`workflow_run_identifier`. Provide a `webhook` URL to receive notifications when the execution
completes. The webhook receives two events: `initialized` (run started) and `finished`/`failed` (run completed).

The webhook payload for a completed run includes a `result` object containing `images`, `videos`,
and `audios` arrays with download URLs for the generated assets.

inputs.description:
Map of input identifier to value. Use each input's `api_key` (recommended) or its `id` (UUID, legacy) as the key — both are accepted.

Value types by input type:
- `creation` (image/media): URL string, base64-encoded string, or existing creation sqid
- `text`: Plain text string
- `number`: Numeric value
- `select`: Value from allowed options

webhook.description:
Optional callback URL that receives status notifications during execution.
The webhook receives POST requests with the event payload (see webhook event schema).
Events are sent when the run starts (`initialized`) and when it finishes (`finished` or `failed`).

endpoints.summary: Change Camera - Transform image perspective
endpoints.description:
Transform an image by changing the camera angle using AI. Adjust horizontal rotation (0-360 degrees), vertical tilt (-30 to 90 degrees), and zoom level (0-10) to generate a new image as if the camera had been repositioned around the subject.

This is an asynchronous endpoint. After submitting a request, use the task ID to poll for results or provide a `webhook_url` to receive a notification when processing completes.

**Camera controls:**
- **Horizontal angle** (`horizontal_angle`): Rotate the viewpoint 0-360 degrees around the subject. `0` = front view, `90` = right side, `180` = back view, `270` = left side.
- **Vertical angle** (`vertical_angle`): Tilt the camera from -30 (looking up) to 90 (bird's eye view). `0` = eye level.
- **Zoom** (`zoom`): Adjust from `0` (wide shot, full scene) to `10` (close-up).

**Use cases:** Product photography with multiple angle views, architectural visualization, creative image manipulation, and generating consistent multi-angle views of objects and scenes.

image.description:
Input image to transform. Provide as a publicly accessible HTTPS URL.
Supported formats: JPG, PNG, WebP.

horizontal_angle.description:
Horizontal rotation angle in degrees. Controls the left-right rotation of the camera around the subject.
- `0`: Front view (no rotation)
- `90`: Right side view
- `180`: Back view
- `270`: Left side view
- `360`: Full rotation (equivalent to 0)

Valid values: `0` to `360`. Default: `0`.

vertical_angle.description:
Vertical tilt angle in degrees. Controls the up-down tilt of the camera relative to the subject.
- `-30`: Looking up at the subject from below
- `0`: Eye-level view (no tilt)
- `45`: Moderate downward angle
- `90`: Bird's eye view (directly above)

Valid values: `-30` to `90`. Default: `0`.

zoom.description:
Zoom level controlling how close the camera appears to the subject.
- `0`: Wide shot (far away, full scene visible)
- `5`: Medium shot (standard framing)
- `10`: Close-up (very close to the subject)

Valid values: `0` to `10`. Default: `5`.

output_format.description:
Output image format.
- `png`: Lossless compression, best for high-quality results
- `jpeg`: Lossy compression, smaller file size suitable for web use

endpoints.summary: Flux Pro - Expand image
endpoints.description:
This endpoint allows you to expand an image using the AI Flux Pro model. The image will be expanded based on the provided parameters.

### Input size

The image you send must be **at least 256 pixels on each side** and **no
larger than 20 megapixels** (`width * height <= 20,000,000`). Neither side
is capped on its own and there is no aspect ratio restriction: a 30000x600
image is accepted, while a 255x70500 one is rejected because one of its
sides is below 256, even though it is only 18 megapixels.

File size is irrelevant — what counts is the decoded pixel count, so a
heavily compressed 60 megapixel photo is rejected just the same. An image
outside these bounds is rejected with an error naming the rule it broke.

Sending more than 20 megapixels buys you nothing anyway: the output is
capped at roughly 1.6 megapixels regardless of how large the input was, so
resize before uploading.

### Output size

`left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` describe the expansion you are asking for,
but **this model does not guarantee that exact output size**. The requested
canvas is `input_width + left + right` by `input_height + top + bottom`, and
two rules are then applied to it:

1. **Maximum output size of roughly 1.6 megapixels.** If the requested canvas
   is larger, the whole image is scaled down proportionally until it fits. The
   aspect ratio is preserved, so there is no single maximum width or height:
   the cap applies to the total pixel count. A 1200x400 image expanded by 400
   pixels on each edge asks for a 2000x1200 canvas and comes back as 1632x976.
2. **Each side is rounded to the nearest multiple of 16.** A requested
   916x692 comes back as 912x688; a requested 936x712 comes back as 944x720.

Both rules apply on every request, including small ones, so an output that
matches your requested pixels exactly is the exception rather than the rule.

Omitting an edge applies its default (512 left, 512 right, 256 top, 256
bottom). Sending `0` leaves that edge unexpanded; sending `0` on all four
edges returns a `400`, since there is nothing to expand.

That said, **this is the expand endpoint that stays closest to the pixel
values you request**: below the 1.6 megapixel cap, the rounding to 16 is the
only deviation. Expanding an 896x672 image by 500 pixels on the top edge
alone asks for 896x1172 and returns 896x1168. The other two expand endpoints
diverge much further:
`ideogram` always renders at about 1 megapixel and only preserves the aspect
ratio, and `seedream-v4-5` scales any canvas below 3.7 megapixels up. If you
need exact output dimensions, resize the result yourself after generation.

image.description: Base64 image to expand

prompt.description: The description of the changes you want to make. This text guides the expansion process, allowing you to specify features, styles, or modifications for the expanded areas.

right.description:
Pixels to expand on the right. Omit the field to use the default of `512`;
send `0` to leave this edge unexpanded.

top.description:
Pixels to expand on the top. Omit the field to use the default of `256`;
send `0` to leave this edge unexpanded.

Pixels to expand on the bottom. Omit the field to use the default of `256`;
send `0` to leave this edge unexpanded.

endpoints.summary: Ideogram - Expand image
endpoints.description:
This endpoint allows you to expand an image using the Ideogram AI model. The image will be expanded based on the provided pixel values for each side.
If no prompt is provided, the model will auto-generate one based on the image content.

### Output size

`left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` define the **aspect ratio** of the result,
not its pixel dimensions. The canvas is built as
`input_width + left + right` by `input_height + top + bottom`, and the model
then renders it at **approximately 1 megapixel**, picking the closest match
from its own fixed list of supported resolutions (all multiples of 32). The
pixel values you send are therefore not preserved:

| Requested canvas | Actual output |
| --- | --- |
| 896x1172 | 832x1088 |
| 1396x672 | 1472x704 |
| 896x896 | 1024x1024 |
| 4992x4768 | 1024x960 |

As the last row shows, a very large expansion does not produce a larger image:
it only changes the shape. If you need specific output dimensions, resize the
result yourself after generation.

`left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` are all required. At least one of them
must be greater than `0`, otherwise the request returns a `400`; the other
three may be `0`.

image.description: Base64 image to expand

prompt.description: Optional text prompt describing the desired expanded content. If not provided, the AI model will auto-generate a prompt based on the image.

left.description: Number of pixels to expand on the left side

right.description: Number of pixels to expand on the right side

top.description: Number of pixels to expand on the top side

bottom.description: Number of pixels to expand on the bottom side

endpoints.summary: Seedream V4.5 - Expand image
endpoints.description:
This endpoint allows you to expand an image using the Seedream V4.5 AI model. The image will be expanded based on the provided pixel values for each side.
If no prompt is provided, the model will auto-generate one based on the image content.

### Output size

The requested canvas is `input_width + left + right` by
`input_height + top + bottom`, and this model constrains it in two ways:

1. **Each side is rounded up to the next multiple of 16.**
2. **The canvas must contain between 3,686,400 and 16,777,216 pixels.** A
   smaller canvas is scaled **up** to reach the lower bound, and a larger one
   is scaled down to the upper bound. Since the lower bound is close to 3.7
   megapixels, a small input with a small expansion is upscaled — a 896x672
   image expanded by 100px on each edge asks for a 1096x872 canvas and comes
   back at 2160x1728, close to twice the requested dimensions (measured).

If you need the output to stay close to the pixel values you requested, use
`POST /v1/ai/image-expand/flux-pro`, which only deviates by the rounding to 16
while the result stays under 1.6 megapixels. For exact dimensions, resize the
result yourself after generation.

`left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` are all required, and at least one of them
must be greater than `0`.

endpoints.description: Relight an image using AI. This endpoint accepts a variety of parameters to customize the generated images.

image.description: Base64 or URL of the image to do the relight

prompt.description:
You can guide the generation process and influence the light transfer with a descriptive prompt. For example, if the reference image is a brightly lit scene, adding something like "A sunlit forest clearing at golden hour" will be helpful.

You can also use your imagination to alter lighting conditions in images: transforming a daytime scene into a moonlit night, enhancing the warmth of a sunset, or even dramatic changes like casting shadows of towering structures across a cityscape.

IMPORTANT: You can emphasize specific aspects of the light in your prompt by using a number in parentheses, ranging from 1 to 1.4, like "(dark scene:1.3)".

transfer_light_from_reference_image.description: Base64 or URL of the reference image for light transfer. Incompatible with 'transfer_light_from_lightmap'

transfer_light_from_lightmap.description: Base64 or URL of the lightmap for light transfer. Icompatible with 'transfer_light_from_reference_image'

light_transfer_strength.description:
It allows you to specify the level of light transfer, meaning the intensity that your prompt, reference image, or lightmap will have. A value of 0% will keep your image closest to the original, while 100% represents the maximum possible light transfer.

If you enable "Interpolate from original", lower values on this slider will make the result even more similar to your original image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `100`

interpolate_from_original.description:
When enabled, this feature will make your final image interpolate from the original using the "Light transfer strength" slider, at the cost of sometimes restricting the generation's freedom.

If disabled, the generation will be freer and will generally produce better results. However, for example, if you want to generate all the frames of a video where a room transitions from having the lights off and very dim lighting to gradually becoming fully illuminated as a new day begins, activating this option might be useful (together with gradually ingreasing the "Light transfer strength" slider).

change_background.description: When enabled, it will change the background based on your prompt and/or reference image. This is super useful for product placement and portraits. However, don't forget to disable it if your scene is something like a landscape or an interior.

preserve_details.description: It will try to maintain the texture and small details of the original image. Especially good for product photography, texts, etc. Disable it if you prefer a smoother result.

whites.description:
Adjust the level of white color in the image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `50`.

blacks.description:
Adjust the level of black color in the image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `50`.

brightness.description:
Adjust the level of brightness in the image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `50`.

contrast.description:
Adjust the level of contrast in the image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `50`.

saturation.description:
Adjust the level of saturation in the image.
Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `50`.

engine.description:
Balanced: Well-rounded, general-purpose option.
Cool: Brighter with cooler tones.
Real: Aims to enhance photographic quality. Experimental.
Illusio: Optimized for illustrations and drawings.
Fairy: Suited for fantasy-themed images.
Colorful Anime: Ideal for anime, cartoons, and vibrant colors.
Hard Transform: Significantly alters the original image.
Softy: Slightly softer effect, suitable for graphic designs.

transfer_light_a.description: Adjusts the intensity of light transfer. Advanced feature requiring practice to use effectively.

transfer_light_b.description: Also modifies light transfer intensity. Can be combined with the previous control for varied effects. Complex to master but offers more control

Fixed generations are ideal for fine-tuning, as it allows for incremental changes to parameters (such as the prompt) to see subtle variations in the output. When disabled, expect each generation to introduce a degree of randomness, leading to more diverse outcomes.

endpoints.summary: Kling 3.0 Turbo I2V 1080p - Generate video
endpoints.description:
Generate AI video from a first-frame image using Kling 3.0 Turbo at 1080p resolution, a fast image-to-video model from the Kling 3.0 family.

**Features:**
- **Image-to-video**: Animate a static image into a dynamic video
- **Optional prompt**: Guide the motion and animation style with text
- **Resolution**: Fixed 1080p output
- **Duration**: 3-15 seconds

**How it works:**
1. Submit an image (URL or Base64) to use as the first frame, with an optional prompt
2. Receive a task ID to track progress
3. Poll the status endpoint or use a `webhook_url` to get notified when the task completes

endpoints.summary: PixVerse V6 - Create video from image
endpoints.description:
Generate a video from an image using the PixVerse-V6 model.

Compared to PixVerse-V5.5, version 6 adds:
- Flexible duration: any integer from `1` to `15` seconds (previously fixed to `5`, `8` or `10`).
- Optional `last_frame_image`: when provided, PixVerse-V6 generates a transition between `image_url` (first frame) and `last_frame_image` (last frame) in the same endpoint — no separate transition endpoint required.

Existing PixVerse-V5.5 features are kept: native audio (`generate_audio_switch`), multi-clip output (`generate_multi_clip_switch`) and prompt reasoning enhancement (`thinking_type`).

prompt.description: Prompt describing the video to generate.

image_url.description: URL of the image to use as the first frame.

last_frame_image.description:
Optional URL of the image to use as the last frame. When provided,
PixVerse-V6 generates a transition between `image_url` (first frame)
and `last_frame_image` (last frame) within the same endpoint.

aspect_ratio.description: The aspect ratio of the generated video

duration.description:
Duration of the generated video in seconds. PixVerse-V6 accepts any

generate_audio_switch.description: When set to `true`, PixVerse-V6 generates synchronized audio (background music, sound effects, or dialogue) together with the video.

generate_multi_clip_switch.description: When set to `true`, PixVerse-V6 produces multi-clip output with dynamic camera changes within a single generation.

thinking_type.description:
Prompt reasoning enhancement mode. Controls how PixVerse-V5.5 optimizes the input prompt before generation.
 * `enabled` - The model rewrites the prompt automatically for better results.
 * `disabled` - The prompt is used exactly as written, with no rewriting.
 * `auto` - The model decides whether to rewrite the prompt based on the input.

endpoints.summary: WAN 2.7 - Create video from image
endpoints.description:
Generate a video from an image or extend an existing video using WAN 2.7.

**Three generation modes:**
- **First frame**: Provide `start_image_url` alone to animate from a starting image
- **First + last frame**: Provide both `start_image_url` and `end_image_url` for controlled start-to-end animation
- **Video continuation**: Provide `video_url` to extend an existing video, optionally with `end_image_url` as the target ending frame

**Key features:**
- 720P and 1080P resolution support
- Optional audio-guided generation
- Duration range: 2-15 seconds

endpoints.description: This asynchronous endpoint enables image upscaling using advanced AI algorithms. Upon submission, it returns a unique `task_id` which can be used to track the progress of the upscaling process. For real-time production use, include the optional `webhook_url` parameter to receive an automated notification once the task has been completed. This allows for seamless integration and efficient task management without the need for continuous polling.

Base64 image to upscale
The resulted image can't exceed maximum allowed size of 25.3 million pixels.

Increase or decrease AI's creativity.

hdr.description:
Increase or decrease the level of definition and detail.
Valid values range `[-10, 10]`, default `0`.

resemblance.description:
Adjust the level of resemblance to the original image.
Valid values range `[-10, 10]`, default `0`.

fractality.description:
Control the strength of the prompt and intricacy per square pixel.
Valid values range `[-10, 10]`, default `0`.

Upscales an image while adding new visual elements or details (V2).
This endpoint may modify the original image content based on the prompt and inferred context.

image.description:
Source image to upscale. Accepts either:
- A publicly accessible HTTPS URL pointing to the image
- A base64-encoded image string

This image will be enhanced with AI-powered upscaling technology that intelligently adds details and improves image quality while increasing resolution.

webhook_url.description:
Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications when the upscaling task completes.
The webhook will be called with the task status and the upscaled image URL.

sharpen.description:
Image sharpness intensity control. Higher values increase edge definition and clarity in the upscaled image.
Valid values range from 0 (no sharpening) to 100 (maximum sharpness). Default is 7.

smart_grain.description:
Intelligent grain/texture enhancement for the upscaled image. Helps preserve natural film grain and texture detail.
Higher values add more fine-grained texture to prevent the upscaled image from looking too smooth or artificial.
Valid values range from 0 (no grain) to 100 (maximum grain). Default is 7.

ultra_detail.description:
Ultra detail enhancement level for the image upscaling process. This parameter controls how much fine detail
the AI adds to the upscaled image, such as textures, patterns, and micro-details.
Higher values create more intricate details. Valid values range from 0 to 100. Default is 30.

flavor.description:
Image processing flavor that determines the upscaling style and optimization for different image types:
- `sublime`: Optimized for artistic and illustrated images with smooth gradients and vibrant colors
- `photo`: Optimized for photographic images, preserving natural colors and realistic details
- `photo_denoiser`: Specialized for photos with noise reduction, ideal for low-light or grainy photographs

scale_factor.description:
Image scaling factor for upscaling. Determines how much larger the output image will be compared to the input.
For example, a scale ratio of 2 will double the dimensions (2x width and 2x height, resulting in 4x total pixels).
Valid values range from 2 to 16. Can be provided as an integer or string.

filter_nsfw.description: Enable NSFW content filtering on the output image

endpoints.summary: Create image from text - Magnific One
endpoints.description:
Generate images with Magnific One, Magnific's image model with art
direction built in: from a prompt, it develops the composition, style,
lighting and visual treatment before rendering.

**Modes:**
- `quality` (default): one finished image, with selectable `quality`
  and `resolution` (up to 4k)
- `draft`: a contact sheet of quick variations, returned as 8 or 16
  individual images — explore directions, then render the chosen one
  in `quality` mode

**Key Features:**
- Art direction from a short prompt
- Optional style reference images (up to 10), in both modes
- 10 aspect ratios, from `21:9` to `9:16`

**Output:** the task's `generated` array holds one image URL in
`quality` mode, or 8 or 16 URLs (one per individual image) in `draft`
mode.

**Credits:** a `quality` request is billed once, at the price of its
`quality` and `resolution`. A `draft` request is billed once for the
whole sheet, at the `medium` / `2k` price, never per image. Reference
images do not change the price.

The request is processed asynchronously: the endpoint returns a task id
immediately. Retrieve the result by polling the task endpoint or by
providing an optional `webhook_url`.

prompt.description:
Text description of the image you want to generate. Magnific One
develops the art direction (composition, style, lighting and visual
treatment) from it before rendering.

**Examples:**
- Simple: "A lighthouse on a cliff at dusk"
- Detailed: "Editorial photo of a lighthouse on a basalt cliff at dusk, long exposure sea, warm window light, cinematic framing"

mode.description:
What the request produces.
- `quality`: one finished image (default)
- `draft`: a contact sheet of quick variations, returned as 8 or 16
  individual images (see `tiles`). Use it to explore directions before
  rendering the chosen one in `quality` mode.

aspect_ratio.description:
Aspect ratio of the image. In `draft` mode it describes each individual
image, not the contact sheet.

With `tiles: 16` every ratio is honoured exactly. With `tiles: 8` the
sheet is twice as wide relative to its images, and the ratios that no
longer fit are approximated to the closest supported one: `1:1`, `2:3`,
`3:2` and `3:4` come back exact, the rest may deviate. Use `tiles: 16`
when the ratio of every image must be exact.

quality.description:
Render quality in `quality` mode.
- `medium`: faster and cheaper
- `high`: maximum detail (default)

Ignored in `draft` mode, which always renders at `medium`.

**Credits:** together with `resolution`, it sets the price of the
request.

resolution.description:
Resolution tier of the image in `quality` mode. Combined with
`aspect_ratio` it selects the exact pixel size.

Ignored in `draft` mode, which always renders its contact sheet at `2k`.

**Credits:** together with `quality`, it sets the price of the request.

tiles.description:
Number of individual images returned in `draft` mode. Ignored in
`quality` mode.
- `8`: a 2x4 sheet (default). May approximate `aspect_ratio`
- `16`: a 4x4 sheet. Always preserves `aspect_ratio` exactly

reference_images.description:
Optional reference images that guide the style of the result.
Supported in both modes. They do not change the price.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

endpoints.summary: Mystic - Create image from text
endpoints.description: Convert descriptive text input into images using AI. This endpoint accepts a variety of parameters to customize the generated images.

schema.description:
### Model Compatibility and LoRA Usage

The Mystic API supports different model configurations with varying LoRA compatibility:

**LoRA-Compatible Configuration:**
- Use the default model (no `model` field specified)
- No `structure_reference` or `style_reference` provided
- LoRAs can be used via:
  - Character syntax in prompt: `@character_name` or `@character_name::strength`
  - `styling.characters` array
  - `styling.styles` array

**LoRA-Incompatible Configurations:**
- **Specific Models**: `fluid`, `flexible` , `super_real` and `editorial_portraits` models ignore all LoRAs
- **Structure Reference**: When `structure_reference` is provided, LoRAs are ignored
- **Style Reference**: When `style_reference` is provided, LoRAs are ignored
- **Combined References**: When both `structure_reference` and `style_reference` are provided, LoRAs are ignored

**Important**: The API will not return errors for incompatible combinations. Instead, LoRAs will be silently ignored, and the request will proceed with the selected model configuration.

prompt.description:
### AI Model Prompt Description

The prompt is a short text that describes the image you want to generate. It can range from simple descriptions, like `"a cat"`, to detailed scenarios, such as `"a cat with wings, playing the guitar, and wearing a hat"`. If no prompt is provided, the AI will generate a random image.

#### Adding Characters to the Prompt
You can introduce characters into the prompt using the following syntax:
- `@character_name`: Represents the character you want to include.
  Example: `My friend @john is a great artist.`

#### Modifying Character Strength
To adjust the influence or "strength" of a character in the image, use the following syntax:
- `@character_name::strength`: Specify the character's strength by appending `::strength` to their name, where `strength` is a numerical value.
  Example: `My friend @john::200 is a great artist.`

Higher strength values will make the character more prominent in the generated image.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

structure_reference.description:
### Structure Reference
Base64 image to use as structure reference. Using images as structure references allows you to influence the shape of your final image. This feature enables various creative applications such as coloring sketches, transforming cartoons into realistic images, texturing basic 3D models, or converting real images into cartoons. The outcome is entirely controlled by your prompt, offering limitless creative possibilities.

structure_strength.description:
Note: This parameter only takes effect when a `"structure_reference"` image is provided.
Allows to maintain the structure of the original image.

style_reference.description:
### Style Reference
Base64 image to use as style reference. Using images as style references allows you to influence the aesthetic of your creation. This is possibly the most powerful tool of Mystic, as it truly lets you create incredibly unique images.

adherence.description:
Note: This parameter only takes effect when a `"style_reference"` image is provided.
Increasing this value will make your generation more faithful to the prompt, but it may transfer the style a bit less accurately. Higher values can help fix small artifacts, anatomical errors and text readability. Lower values will give you more creative images and closer to the style reference.

hdr.description:
Note: This parameter only takes effect when a `"style_reference"` image is provided.
Increasing this value can give you a more detailed image, at the cost of a more 'AI look' and slightly worse style transfer. Lower values have a more natural and artistic look but may increase artifacts.

resolution.description: Resolution of the image

aspect_ratio.description:
Image size with the aspect ratio. The aspect ratio is the proportional relationship between an image's width and height, expressed as *_width_height (e.g., square_1_1, widescreen_16_9). It is calculated by dividing the width by the height.\
If not present, the default is `square_1_1`.
Note: For the `fluid` model, only this values are valid:
* square_1_1
* social_story_9_16
* widescreen_16_9
* traditional_3_4
* classic_4_3

model.description:
* `zen` - for smoother, basic, and cleaner results. Fewer objects in the scene and less intricate details. The softer looking one.

* `flexible` - good prompt adherence. However, it has results that are a bit more HDR and saturated than Realism or Fluid. It's especially good with illustrations, fantastical prompts, and for diving into the latent space in search of very specific visual styles.

* `fluid` - the model that adheres best to prompts with great average quality for all kind of images. It can generate really creative images! It will always follow your input no matter what.

* `realism` - with a more realistic color palette. It tries to give an extra boost of reality to your images, a kind of "less AI look". Works especially well with photographs but also magically works with illustrations too. IMPORTANT: you should use Zen, Flexible or Fluid if you are trying to generate something that is really fantastic or a known character, Realism may not follow your prompt well.

* `super_real` - if reality is your priority, this is your model. Nearly as versatile as Flexible, it excels in realism outperforming Editorial Portraits in medium shots, though not as strong for close-ups.

* `editorial_portraits` - the most amazing state-of-the-art generator for editorial portraits. You have never seen a level of realism like this before. Perfect for hyperrealistic close-up or medium shots. Unfortunately, in wide or distant shots, it generates anatomical problems and artifacts... but for close-ups, it is simply the best on the market. Tip: use the longest and most explanatory prompts possible, they really suit it well!

creative_detailing.description:
Higher values can achieve greater detail per pixel at higher resolutions at the cost of giving a somewhat more "HDR" or artificial look.
Very high values can generate quite crazy things like eyes where they shouldn't appear, etc.

Valid values range `[0, 100]`, default `33`

engine.description:
Select the engine for the AI model. Available options:
  * `automatic` - default choice
  * `Illusio` - for smoother illustrations, landscapes, and nature. The softer looking one.
  * `Sharpy` - better for realistic images like photographs and for a more grainy look. It provides the sharpest and most detailed images. If you use it for illustrations it will give them more texture and a less softer look.
  * `Sparkle` - also good for realistic images. It's a middle ground between Illusio and Sharpy.

fixed_generation.description:
When this option is enabled, using the same settings will consistently produce the same image.
Fixed generations are ideal for fine-tuning, as it allows for incremental changes to parameters (such as the prompt) to see subtle variations in the output.
When disabled, expect each generation to introduce a degree of randomness, leading to more diverse outcomes.

filter_nsfw.description:
Controls **NSFW** (Not Safe For Work) content filtering during generation.

This parameter is always set to `true` by default and NSFW filtering **cannot be disabled** for standard API usage. Only authorized clients with special permissions can disable this filter.

**Important:** If your use case requires disabling NSFW filtering, please contact our support team to discuss your requirements and potential authorization.

name.description:
Name of the style to apply.
**The name of the style can be found in the `v1/ai/loras` endpoint.**

strength.description:
Strength of the style to apply. The higher the value, the more the style will be applied to the image. Some styles may not be affected by this parameter.

Valid values range `[0, 200]`. Default value is `100`.

characters.description: Modify the characters introduced in the `prompt` field adjusting their strength

id.description:
ID of the character to modify.
**This ID can be found in the `v1/ai/loras` endpoint.**

strength.description:
Strength of the character to apply. The higher the value, the more the character will be applied to the image.
If ID is not set, the strength will be applied to the character specified in the `prompt` field.

Valid values range `[0, 200]`. Default value is `100`.

colors.description: Dominant colors to generate the image

endpoints.summary: Happy Horse 1.0 - Create video from reference images
endpoints.description:
Generate a high-quality AI video guided by 1 to 9 reference images that define characters, objects or scenes using Happy Horse 1.0, Alibaba's reference-to-video model.

**How to use references:**
- Provide 1 to 9 reference images via `image_urls`
- Reference each image in the prompt by its 1-based positional index (`character1`, `character2`, ...)
- The order of `image_urls` matches the character index in the prompt

**Key features:**
- 720P and 1080P resolution support
- 5 aspect ratio options
- Duration range: 3-15 seconds
- Optional bottom-right "Happy Horse" watermark
- Prompt up to 5000 characters

schema.description: Generate video guided by 1 to 9 reference images that define characters, objects or scenes using Happy Horse 1.0. In the prompt, reference each image by its 1-based positional index (`character1`, `character2`, ...). The order matches the array order.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

prompt.description:
Text prompt describing the desired elements and visual style of the generated video. Supports any language. Requests with prompts longer than 5000 characters are rejected by validation; the upstream provider further treats 5000 non-Chinese characters or 2500 Chinese characters as the effective ceiling.

Use `character1`, `character2`, ... in the prompt to reference the corresponding image in the `image_urls` array; the order matches the array order.

**Example:** "character1 and character2 walk together through a sunlit forest path"

image_urls.description:
Ordered array of reference images. Array position determines the character reference number in the prompt (1st item → `character1`, 2nd → `character2`, etc.).

**Supported formats:** JPEG, JPG, PNG, WEBP
**Recommended resolution:** shortest side at least 400 px (720P or higher recommended)
**Maximum file size:** 10 MB per image

items.description: A reference image used to guide reference-to-video generation.

url.description:
Publicly accessible URL of the reference image.

**Supported formats:** JPEG, JPG, PNG, WEBP
**Recommended resolution:** shortest side at least 400 px (720P or higher recommended)
**Maximum file size:** 10 MB

aspect_ratio.description:
Output video aspect ratio:
- `16:9`: Landscape (widescreen)
- `9:16`: Portrait (vertical, mobile-optimized)
- `1:1`: Square
- `4:3`: Standard landscape
- `3:4`: Standard portrait

resolution.description:

- `720P`: 720p HD (1280x720)
- `1080P`: 1080p Full HD (1920x1080)

duration.description: Duration of the generated video in seconds.

watermark.description: Whether to add a watermark to the generated video. The watermark appears in the bottom-right corner with the fixed text "Happy Horse".

seed.description: Random seed for reproducibility. Use the same seed with identical parameters to improve reproducibility (does not guarantee identical results). Leave unset for a random seed.

endpoints.summary: Kling 3 Omni Pro - Video-to-video generation
endpoints.description:
Generate AI video using Kling 3 Omni Pro with a reference video for motion and style guidance.

**Video-to-video mode:** This endpoint requires a `video_url` parameter. Reference the video in your prompt using `@Video1`.

**Features:**
- Use a reference video (3-10s) to guide motion and style
- Combine with an image for start frame control
- High-quality pro output

**Use case:** Create videos that follow motion patterns from a reference video while applying your creative prompt.

**Duration:** 3-15 seconds
**Quality:** Pro mode offers highest quality output.

**Tip:** For text-to-video or image-to-video without a reference video, use the `/ai/video/kling-v3-omni-pro` endpoint instead.

cfg_scale.description:

Values above 1 are not supported for Kling 3 (only Kling 1.x models support cfg_scale up to 2).

- **0**: Maximum creative freedom, loosest interpretation of the prompt
- **0.5** (default): Balanced between prompt adherence and creativity
- **1**: Strongest adherence to the prompt, least creative variation

endpoints.summary: Create image from text - Ideogram 4
endpoints.description:
Generate images from text with Ideogram 4.

**Key Features:**
- Accurate text rendering for posters, logos and typography
- 15 aspect ratios, from `3:1` to `1:3`, always at about 4 megapixels
- Optional negative prompt, Magic Prompt control and seed

**Best for:**
- Posters, flyers and social graphics with legible text
- Logos and typographic designs

**Credits:** the price is set by `rendering_speed` (`TURBO`, `DEFAULT` or
`QUALITY`). The other parameters do not affect it.

prompt.description:
Text description of the image to generate. Ideogram 4 is especially good
at rendering text: put the words to draw in quotes.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

negative_prompt.description:
What to leave out of the image. Descriptions in `prompt` take precedence
over this field.

aspect_ratio.description:
Aspect ratio for the generated image. The output is always about 4
megapixels: 2048x2048 at `1:1`, and the same area at the other ratios.

**Available ratios:**
- `1:1`: Square (default)
- `16:9`, `9:16`: Widescreen/Social stories
- `16:10`, `10:16`: Widescreen/Tall
- `4:3`, `3:4`: Standard
- `3:2`, `2:3`: Classic photo
- `5:4`, `4:5`: Photo print
- `2:1`, `1:2`, `3:1`, `1:3`: Banners and vertical panels

rendering_speed.description:
Quality tier. It sets the price of the generation.

**Available tiers:**
- `TURBO`: Fastest and cheapest
- `DEFAULT`: Balanced quality and speed (default)
- `QUALITY`: Highest quality, slowest

magic_prompt.description:
Whether Ideogram's Magic Prompt rewrites the prompt into a more detailed
one before generating. `AUTO` lets the model decide; use `OFF` to render
the prompt verbatim. It does not affect the price.

seed.description: Seed for reproducible results. When omitted, a random seed is used.

endpoints.summary: Create image from text - Ideogram 4.5
endpoints.description:
Generate or edit images with Ideogram 4.5.

**Key Features:**
- Text-to-image and image editing in the same endpoint: send up to 5
  images; the first one is edited and the rest guide the edit
- Accurate text rendering for posters, logos and typography
- 13 aspect ratios at about 4 megapixels, plus `auto` to follow the
  input image

**Best for:**
- Designs with legible text, from scratch or from an existing image
- Instruction-based edits of an image guided by references

**Credits:** the price is set by `quality` (`very_low`, `low`, `medium` or
`high`). The other parameters do not affect it. `very_low` is only
available when images are sent.

prompt.description:
Text description of the image to generate, or of the edit to apply. When
`images` are sent, refer to them by position: "image 1" is the first one
(the image being edited) and "image 2" onwards are the references.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

images.description:
Optional input images. Without them the request is text-to-image. With
them, the first image is the one being edited and the rest guide the
edit as references.

**Image requirements:**
- Maximum 5 images
- Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP
- Aspect ratio between 1:6 and 6:1
- Public HTTPS URL or base64-encoded string

aspect_ratio.description:
Aspect ratio for the generated image, on a canvas of about 4 megapixels.

**Available ratios:**
- `auto`: Let the model choose (default). With `images` it follows the
  first image; without them it picks the canvas that best fits the prompt.
- `1:1`: Square, 2048x2048
- `4:5`, `5:4`: Photo print
- `3:4`, `4:3`: Standard
- `2:3`, `3:2`: Classic photo
- `9:16`, `16:9`: Social stories/Widescreen
- `1:2`, `2:1`, `1:3`, `3:1`: Banners and vertical panels

quality.description:
Quality tier. It sets the price of the generation.

**Available tiers:**
- `very_low`: Cheapest and fastest. Only available when `images` are sent
  (editing); a text-only request with it is rejected.
- `low`
- `medium`: Default
- `high`: Best quality, slowest

magic_prompt.description:
Whether Ideogram's Magic Prompt rewrites the prompt into a more detailed
one before generating. `auto` lets the model decide; use `off` for
verbatim edit instructions. It does not affect the price.

seed.description: Seed for reproducible results. When omitted, a random seed is used.

  reference images to edit, combine, or keep characters and products
  consistent
- Wide aspect ratio range, from `8:1` banners to `1:8` vertical strips,

- Optional `thinking_level` for complex prompts
- Optional Google Search grounding

**Best for:**

- Character and product consistency across generations
- Complex prompts with many constraints

and product consistency.

endpoints.summary: Create image from text - Recraft V4
endpoints.description:
Generate an image from a text prompt using Recraft V4.

**Key Features:**
- Best-in-class rendering of legible text inside the image
- Design-oriented output: posters, signage, packaging, editorial layouts
- Eleven fixed aspect ratios, from 768x1344 to 1536x768

**Best for:**
- Designs whose wording must be readable and correctly spelled
- Brand and marketing assets with typographic weight

**Output:** one image per request, delivered as a URL in the task's
`generated` array. Exact sizes are listed under `aspect_ratio`.

**Credits:** a flat price per image. Recraft V4 Pro renders the same
sizes at twice the linear dimensions for a higher price.

The request is processed asynchronously: the endpoint returns a task id
immediately. Retrieve the result by polling the task endpoint or by
providing an optional `webhook_url`.

prompt.description:
Text description of the image you want to generate.

**Tips:**
- Recraft's strength is rendering legible text inside the image, so spell
  out any wording the design must contain
- Describe layout, palette and typography, not just the subject

**Examples:**
- Simple: "A storefront sign that reads OPEN DAILY 9AM"
- Detailed: "A storefront sign that reads OPEN DAILY 9AM, flat vector poster style, cream and navy palette, bold rounded display type"

aspect_ratio.description:
Aspect ratio of the generated image, expressed as *_width_height.

Recraft renders from a fixed set of sizes, so the output dimensions are the
ones listed below and are **not always the exact mathematical ratio the
name suggests** — `widescreen_16_9` renders 1344x768, which is 7:4.

| `aspect_ratio` | V4 / V4.1 `mid` | V4 Pro / V4.1 `pro` |
|---|---|---|
| `square_1_1` | 1024x1024 | 2048x2048 |
| `horizontal_2_1` | 1536x768 | 3072x1536 |
| `vertical_1_2` | 768x1536 | 1536x3072 |
| `standard_3_2` | 1280x832 | 2560x1664 |
| `portrait_2_3` | 832x1280 | 1664x2560 |
| `classic_4_3` | 1216x896 | 2432x1792 |
| `traditional_3_4` | 896x1216 | 1792x2432 |
| `social_5_4` | 1152x896 | 2304x1792 |
| `social_post_4_5` | 896x1152 | 1792x2304 |
| `widescreen_16_9` | 1344x768 | 2688x1536 |
| `social_story_9_16` | 768x1344 | 1536x2688 |

enhance_prompt.description:
Rewrite the prompt with an LLM before generating, which generally produces
a richer design. Any text the image must render is preserved verbatim.

Set it to `false` to send the prompt exactly as written, which is what you
want when you need a deterministic input.

endpoints.summary: Request pre-signed URLs to upload files
endpoints.description:
Request one or more pre-signed URLs to upload your own files (image, video or audio) and reference them in other AI endpoints.

Flow:
1. Call this endpoint with the `content_type` of each file. You get, per file, an `upload_url` (pre-signed PUT), an opaque `file_id`, and a readable `asset_url`.
2. PUT the raw file bytes to each `upload_url`, including ALL the returned `headers`. The `upload_url` expires quickly (`expires_in`).
3. Reference the upload by `file_id` (preferred on AI endpoints) or by `asset_url` (a plain URL usable anywhere a URL is accepted).

endpoints.summary: Happy Horse 1.0 - Edit video
endpoints.description:
Edit an existing video with natural-language instructions using Happy Horse 1.0, Alibaba's AI video editing model, optionally guided by up to 5 reference images.

**Editing modes:**
- **Instruction-based editing**: Provide `prompt` with editing instructions (e.g., "change the sky to sunset")
- **Reference-image editing**: Provide `prompt` and `image_urls`, then reference images from the prompt using `@Image1`..`@Image5` (1-based, in array order)

**Key features:**
- 720P and 1080P resolution support
- Up to 5 reference images
- Output is capped at 15 seconds
- Configurable audio handling: `auto` (regenerate when relevant) or `origin` (preserve input audio)

endpoints.summary: Video Upscaler - Upscale video
endpoints.description:
Upscales a video while enhancing visual quality and resolution.
Supports various output resolutions (720p, 1k, 2k, 4k) with optional creativity, sharpening, and grain controls.

video.description: Source video to upscale. Must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL pointing to the video.

creativity.description:
Creativity intensity. Controls how much creative freedom is applied during upscaling.
Valid values range from 0 (no creativity) to 100 (maximum creativity). Default is 0.

resolution.description:
Output resolution for the video upscaling:
- `720p`: HD output
- `1k`: Standard definition output
- `2k`: High definition output (default)
- `4k`: Ultra high definition output

fps_boost.description: Enable FPS boost to increase the frame rate of the upscaled video.

sharpen.description:
Video sharpness intensity control. Higher values increase edge definition and clarity.
Valid values range from 0 (no sharpening) to 100 (maximum sharpness). Default is 0.

smart_grain.description:
Applies a film grain effect to the output video. Helps preserve natural film grain and texture detail.
Valid values range from 0 (no grain) to 100 (maximum grain). Default is 0.

flavor.description:
Video processing flavor that determines the upscaling style:
- `vivid`: Enhanced colors and contrast for more vibrant output
- `natural`: Preserves original colors and natural appearance

output_format.description:
Output video format. `h264` (default) returns an H.264 MP4. `prores_422_hq` returns an Apple ProRes 422 HQ master (.mov) alongside an H.264 preview.
When `prores_422_hq` is selected the completed task's `generated` array contains both files: the H.264 MP4 preview and the ProRes master, which can be identified by its `.mov` extension.

webhook_url.description:
Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications when the upscaling task completes.
The webhook will be called with the task status and the upscaled video URL.

A value of 0 returns the original video, 100 returns the fully upscaled result.

Guidance scale controlling prompt adherence versus creative freedom. Range: 0 to 1.

● The aspect ratio of the mask image MUST match the input image (`image` field); otherwise, the task will fail.
● The resolutions of the `static_mask` image and the `dynamic_masks.mask` images must be identical; otherwise, the task will fail.
● The static brush feature allows you to define areas where motion will be applied in the generated video.

mask.description:

● Support inputting image Base64 encoding or image URL (ensure the URL is accessible and follows the same format requirements as the image field).

Note: This parameter maps to Kling's internal "intelligence" spelling for the intelligent option.
Defaults to "customize" when multi_prompt is provided.

**Note:** When using multi-shot mode, total duration across all shots cannot exceed 15 seconds.

negative_prompt.description: Undesired elements to avoid in the generated video. Maximum 2500 characters.

cfg_scale.description:

- **0.5** (default): Balanced between prompt adherence and creativity
- **1**: Strongest adherence to the prompt, least creative variation

endpoints.summary: MiniMax H3 2K - Create video
endpoints.description: Generate 2K video with MiniMax H3. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video with an optional first and last frame, and subject reference images (up to 9, mentioned in the prompt as @Image1..@Image9). Keyframes and reference images are mutually exclusive. The response is a task: poll the GET endpoint or supply `webhook_url` to be notified; the finished task carries a time-limited MP4 URL. Reference videos are billed on top of the output duration, capped at 15 seconds.

webhook_url.description: URL to receive a webhook notification when the video generation task completes. The webhook payload includes the task ID and status.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video to generate. Chinese and English are supported. Mention reference images as @Image1, @Image2, ... matching their 1-indexed array order. For best instruction following keep it under roughly 500 Chinese characters or 1,000 English words.

image.description: Optional image to use as the first frame for image-to-video generation. Accepts a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images`.

image_end.description: Optional image to use as the last frame for image-to-video generation. Requires `image`: the provider rejects a last frame with no first frame. Together they generate a transition video between the two. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images`. Accepts a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image.

reference_images.description: Up to 9 reference images for reference-to-video generation. Each item is a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Reference them in the prompt using @Image1, @Image2, ... @Image9 (1-indexed to the array order). Each image must be JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC or HEIF, no larger than 30 MB, 256 to 5760 px per side, with an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

reference_videos.description: Up to 3 reference videos. Each item must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or a video upload file_id (`upl_vid_...`). Reference them in the prompt using @Video1, @Video2 or @Video3. Each video must be MP4 or MOV (H.264 or H.265), 2 to 15 seconds, 23.976 to 60 fps, no larger than 50 MB, 256 to 5760 px per side, with an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5, and their combined duration must not exceed 15 seconds. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`. **These are billed**: their combined duration is added to the output duration, capped at 15 seconds.

reference_audios.description: Up to 3 reference audios. Each item must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL — unlike `reference_videos`, this field does not take upload file_ids. Reference them in the prompt using @Audio1, @Audio2 or @Audio3. Each audio must be WAV or MP3, 2 to 15 seconds and no larger than 15 MB, and their combined duration must not exceed 15 seconds. Audio cannot be the only reference: at least one `reference_images` or `reference_videos` entry is required alongside it. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`. Adds nothing to the price.

duration.description: Video duration in seconds. Any integer from 4 to 15. H3 accepts 4-second clips, unlike H3 Max, whose floor is 5.

aspect_ratio.description:
Output video aspect ratio. Available options:
- `adaptive`: infer the ratio from the reference images
- `film_horizontal_21_9`: Ultra-wide cinematic (21:9)
- `widescreen_16_9`: Standard widescreen (16:9)
- `classic_4_3`: Classic TV format (4:3)
- `square_1_1`: Square format (1:1)
- `traditional_3_4`: Portrait classic (3:4)
- `social_story_9_16`: Vertical/social media story (9:16)

**`adaptive` needs something to adapt to.** It only means anything when the request carries `reference_images`; on a text-only request there is nothing to infer from and it falls back to `widescreen_16_9`.

**Note:** ignored when `image` or `image_end` is supplied — in keyframe mode the output always follows the aspect ratio of the supplied image.

aigc_watermark.description: Whether the provider stamps a visible AI-generated-content watermark on the output video.

endpoints.summary: Seedance 2.5 Pro 1080p - Create video from text or image
endpoints.description: Generate 1080p video using Seedance 2.5 Pro. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video (first/last frame), and reference-to-video with up to 30 reference images (@Image1..@Image30), 10 reference videos (@Video1..@Video10) and 10 reference audios (@Audio1..@Audio10). Also supports video editing and extension via `task_type`, camera motion, multishot sequences (up to 6 shots) and native audio (sound effects).

webhook_url.description: URL to receive a webhook notification when the video generation task completes. The webhook payload includes the task ID and status.

image.description: Optional image to use as the first frame for image-to-video generation. Accepts a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images` and `reference_videos`.

image_end.description: Optional image to use as the last frame for image-to-video generation. Requires `image`. When provided together with `image`, the model generates a transition video between the first and last frame. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images` and `reference_videos`.

reference_images.description: Up to 30 reference images (subjects, characters, products or style references). Each item is a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Reference them in the prompt using @Image1, @Image2, ... @Image30 (1-indexed to the array order). Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

reference_videos.description: Up to 10 reference videos. Each item must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or a video upload file_id (`upl_vid_...`). Reference them in the prompt using @Video1, @Video2, ... @Video10 (1-indexed to the array order). Each video must be MP4 or MOV, 2 to 30 seconds, 24 to 60 fps, no larger than 200 MB, with 409600 to 8295044 pixels and an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5. Combined duration must not exceed 30 seconds. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

reference_audios.description:
Up to 10 reference audios (2-60s each, mp3 or wav). Each item is a publicly accessible URL: unlike `reference_images`, this field does not take upload file_ids. Reference them in the prompt using @Audio1, @Audio2, ... @Audio10 (1-indexed to the array order).

**The audio is not copied into the video.** The model composes its own soundtrack, guided by the rhythm and character of what you send: a 120 BPM reference produces a soundtrack at that tempo, but it is a new recording, not your file muxed into the result. A reference with a clear beat, music or speech gives the model something to follow; a flat tone or near-silence does not.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video to generate. To use references, mention them as @Image1, @Video1, @Audio1, ... matching the 1-indexed order of each reference array. Maximum 40000 characters. Prompts longer than 5,000 characters are accepted, but results may become less predictable.

task_type.description: How the reference videos are used. Setting any value requires at least one reference video; without one the request is rejected with 400. When the field is omitted, a request WITH reference videos behaves as `reference`, and a request without them is plain generation (the field plays no part). `reference` generates a NEW video guided by the references. `edit` modifies the source video named in the prompt: the output keeps that video's aspect ratio and duration, so `duration` must be omitted and `aspect_ratio` must be omitted or `adaptive`; billing uses the measured duration of the longest reference video as the output seconds, plus the usual reference-video surcharge. `extend` continues the source video: the output is the generated continuation and lasts `duration` seconds (default 5) with the source video's aspect ratio, so `aspect_ratio` must be omitted or `adaptive`; billing uses `duration` plus the reference surcharge. `auto` lets the model infer the task from the prompt; the request is sent exactly as given, with no server-side defaults for `duration` or `aspect_ratio`, and when `duration` is omitted billing assumes the output follows the longest reference video. Requests that violate these constraints are rejected with 400 and the offending field named in `invalid_params`, before any credits are consumed.

duration.description: Video duration in seconds. Any integer from 4 to 30. When omitted the server applies 5, with two exceptions: with `task_type: edit` the field must not be sent at all (the output keeps the source video's duration; sending it returns 400), and with `task_type: auto` no default is applied (nothing is dispatched and the model decides). The default is applied server-side, not declared in the schema, so generated clients no longer auto-fill it — the API behaviour for an omitted value is unchanged.

aspect_ratio.description: Output video aspect ratio, per task. Text-to-video and reference-to-video generation: defaults to `widescreen_16_9`; `adaptive` pins no ratio and lets the model choose from the prompt and references. Image-to-video (`image` first frame): ignored — the output inherits the start frame's ratio. `task_type: edit` or `extend`: the output always follows the source video's ratio, so the field must be omitted or `adaptive`; any fixed value returns 400.

camera_fixed.description: When `true`, the camera position stays fixed (tripod shot). When `false`, the model may apply natural camera movements.

camera_motion.description: Optional camera movement to guide the shot. Each value is expanded into a descriptive instruction appended to the prompt.

multishot.description: Optional multishot sequence of up to 6 shots. When provided, the shots drive the generation and replace the top-level `prompt` (which is still required). If any shot has a `duration`, all shots must have one and the durations must sum to `duration`.

prompt.description: The prompt describing this shot. Prompts longer than 5,000 characters are accepted, but results may become less predictable.

duration.description: Duration of this shot in seconds.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible video generation. Use `-1` for a random seed.

sound_effects.description: Whether to generate native audio (sound effects and ambience) for the video.

no_music.description: Suppress background music in the generated native audio. Only applies when `sound_effects` is enabled.

output_format.description: Container format of the generated video. `mov` trades file size for colour fidelity; `mp4` is the default.

enable_safety_checker.description: Enable content safety filtering to ensure generated videos comply with safety guidelines.

Also supports reference-to-video: attach up to 9 reference images via `reference_images` and mention them in the prompt with @Image1..@Image9.

webhook_url.description: URL to receive a webhook notification when the video generation task completes. The webhook payload includes the task ID and status.

image.description: Optional image to use as the first frame for image-to-video generation. Accepts a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images`, `reference_videos` and `reference_audios`.

image_end.description: Optional image to use as the last frame for image-to-video generation. Requires `image`: the provider rejects a last frame with no first frame. Together they generate a transition video between the two. Mutually exclusive with `reference_images`, `reference_videos` and `reference_audios`. Accepts a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image.

reference_images.description: Up to 9 reference images for reference-to-video generation. Each item is a publicly accessible URL or a base64-encoded image. Reference them in the prompt using @Image1, @Image2, ... @Image9 (1-indexed to the array order). Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

reference_videos.description: Up to 3 reference videos. Each item must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or a video upload file_id (`upl_vid_...`). Reference them in the prompt using @Video1, @Video2, or @Video3. Each video must be MP4 or MOV, 2 to 15 seconds, 24 to 60 fps, no larger than 50 MB, with 409600 to 2086876 pixels and an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5. Combined duration must not exceed 15 seconds. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

reference_audios.description:
Up to 3 reference audios, to guide the generated soundtrack with a voice, a piece of music or an ambience. Each item must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL — unlike `reference_images` and `reference_videos`, this field does not take upload file_ids. Reference them in the prompt using @Audio1, @Audio2, or @Audio3.

**The audio is not copied into the video.** The model composes its own soundtrack, guided by the rhythm and character of what you send: a 120 BPM reference produces a soundtrack at that tempo, but it is a new recording, not your file muxed into the result. A reference with a clear beat, music or speech gives the model something to follow; a flat tone or near-silence does not.

Requirements for each item: MP3 or WAV, 2 to 15 seconds, no larger than 15 MB, and the combined duration of all of them must not exceed 15 seconds.

Requires at least one `reference_images` or `reference_videos` entry — the model rejects a request whose only reference is audio. Mutually exclusive with `image` and `image_end`.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video to generate. Mention references as @Image1, @Image2, ... @Video1, @Video2, ... or @Audio1, @Audio2, ... matching their 1-indexed array order. Maximum 40000 characters. Prompts longer than 5,000 characters are accepted, but results may become less predictable.

duration.description: Video duration in seconds. Any integer from 4 to 15.

aspect_ratio.description:
Output video aspect ratio. Available options:
- `film_horizontal_21_9`: Ultra-wide cinematic (21:9)
- `widescreen_16_9`: Standard widescreen (16:9)
- `classic_4_3`: Classic TV format (4:3)
- `square_1_1`: Square format (1:1)
- `traditional_3_4`: Portrait classic (3:4)
- `social_story_9_16`: Vertical/social media story (9:16)
- `film_vertical_9_21`: Ultra-tall vertical (9:21)

**Note:** This parameter only applies to text-to-video and reference-to-video requests. When an `image` (first frame) is provided for image-to-video generation, `aspect_ratio` is ignored: the output video inherits the aspect ratio of the start frame.

camera_fixed.description: When set to `true`, the camera position stays fixed (tripod shot) throughout the video. When `false`, the model may apply natural camera movements.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible video generation. Use the same seed with the same prompt to get consistent results. Use `-1` for a random seed.

sound_effects.description: Whether to generate native audio (sound effects and ambience) for the video. Set to `false` to generate a silent video. Ignored when `reference_audios` are attached: the reference audio is what the soundtrack is built from.

no_music.description: Suppress background music in the generated native audio. Only applies when `sound_effects` is enabled.

enable_safety_checker.description: Enable content safety filtering to ensure generated videos comply with safety guidelines. When `true`, the model filters unsafe content.

endpoints.summary: VFX - Apply visual effects to video
endpoints.description:
Apply professional visual effects and filters to your videos using the VFX API. Transform any video with cinematic effects like film grain, motion blur, VHS retro style, and anamorphic lens distortion.

**Available filters:**
- `1` Film grain - Adds cinematic grain texture for a classic film look
- `2` Motion blur - Creates motion blur effect (configurable kernel size and decay)
- `3` Fish eye - Applies fish eye lens distortion
- `4` VHS - Retro VHS tape effect with scan lines and color distortion
- `5` Shake - Camera shake effect for dynamic footage
- `6` VGA - Low resolution VGA effect for retro aesthetics
- `7` Bloom - Glowing bloom effect (adjustable contrast)
- `8` Anamorphic lens - Cinematic anamorphic lens effect with horizontal flares

**Use cases:** Social media content, music videos, film production, advertising, retro-style videos, and creative projects.

webhook_url.description: Webhook URL to notify when the task is completed

video.description: URL of the video to apply effects to. Must be publicly accessible.

filter_type.description:
Type of visual effect filter to apply to the video.

**Available filters:**
- `1`: Film grain - Adds cinematic grain texture
- `2`: Motion blur - Creates motion blur effect
- `3`: Fish eye - Applies fish eye lens distortion
- `4`: VHS - Retro VHS tape effect
- `5`: Shake - Camera shake effect
- `6`: VGA - Low resolution VGA effect
- `7`: Bloom - Glowing bloom effect (use bloom_filter_contrast to adjust)
- `8`: Anamorphic lens - Cinematic anamorphic lens effect

fps.description: Frames per second for the output video

bloom_filter_contrast.description: Contrast value for bloom filter effect. Only applicable when filter_type is 7 (bloom).

motion_filter_kernel_size.description: Kernel size for motion blur filter. Only applicable when filter_type is 2 (motion_blur).

motion_filter_decay_factor.description: Decay factor for motion blur filter. Only applicable when filter_type is 2 (motion_blur).

endpoints.summary: Video generation using Wan 3.0
endpoints.description:
Generate a video with Wan 3.0, Alibaba's unified video model. One
endpoint covers every mode, chosen by the fields you send:

- **Text-to-video**: `prompt` only.
- **First/last frame**: `start_image_url`, optionally with `end_image_url`
  (a last frame needs a first frame).
- **References**: up to 10 `image_urls`, 5 `video_urls` and 5 `audio_urls`
  for characters, motion, voice or style. Not combinable with keyframes.

**Output:** one MP4 video of 2 to 30 seconds at 480p, 720p or 1080p (the
short side is 480, 720 or 1080 px, e.g. 854x480 at 16:9), with native
audio by default. The finished task carries the video URL in its
`generated` array.

**Credits:** priced per second by `resolution`. The billed seconds are
`duration` plus the combined duration of the `video_urls`, capped at 15
seconds. Images and audios do not change the price.

The request is processed asynchronously: the endpoint returns a `task_id`
immediately. Retrieve the result by polling
`GET /v1/ai/video/wan-3-0/{task-id}` or by providing an optional `webhook_url`.

schema.description:
Wan 3.0, Alibaba's unified video model. One request covers text-to-video,
first/last frame image-to-video and reference-guided generation from
images, videos and audios. The mode follows from the fields you send.

References (`image_urls`, `video_urls`, `audio_urls`) and keyframes
(`start_image_url`, `end_image_url`) are mutually exclusive: a request
that mixes them is rejected.

**Reference videos are billed.** The provider charges this model as the
output duration PLUS the combined duration of the reference videos,
capped at 15 seconds, and that is what the API charges. Reference images
and audios add nothing to the price.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

prompt.description:
Text description of the video to generate, including action and
dialogue. Chinese and English are supported. Refer to references by
their position in each list: "Image 1" is the first item of
`image_urls`, "Video 1" the first item of `video_urls`, "Audio 1" the
first item of `audio_urls`.

image_urls.description:
Up to 10 reference images for characters, objects, scenes or style.
Each item is a public HTTPS URL, a base64-encoded image or an upload
id (`upl_...`). JPEG, PNG (no alpha channel), BMP or WEBP, at most
20 MB, 240 to 8000 px per side, aspect ratio up to 8:1. Mutually
exclusive with `start_image_url` and `end_image_url`.

video_urls.description:
Up to 5 reference videos for motion, appearance or voice. Each item is
a public HTTPS URL or a video upload id (`upl_vid_...`). MP4 or MOV,
1 to 15 seconds each and at most 15 seconds combined, at most 100 MB,
240 to 4096 px per side, aspect ratio up to 8:1. The combined
duration plus `duration` must not exceed 30 seconds. Mutually
exclusive with `start_image_url` and `end_image_url`.

**These are billed**: their combined duration is added to the output
duration, capped at 15 seconds.

audio_urls.description:
Up to 5 reference audios for voice timbre or soundtrack. Each item is
a public HTTPS URL. WAV or MP3, 1 to 15 seconds each and at most 15
seconds combined, at most 15 MB. Mutually exclusive with
`start_image_url` and `end_image_url`. Adds nothing to the price.

start_image_url.description:
Optional first frame of the video. A public HTTPS URL, a base64-encoded
image or an upload id (`upl_...`). When supplied, the output follows
the aspect ratio of this image and `aspect_ratio` is ignored. JPEG,
PNG (no alpha channel), BMP or WEBP, at most 20 MB, 240 to 8000 px
per side. Mutually exclusive with every reference field.

end_image_url.description:
Optional last frame of the video. Requires `start_image_url`: the
provider rejects a last frame with no first frame. Same formats and limits as
`start_image_url`. Mutually exclusive with every reference field.

aspect_ratio.description:
Output video aspect ratio. Defaults to `16:9` when not specified.
Ignored when `start_image_url` is supplied: the output then follows the
aspect ratio of that image.
- `16:9`: Landscape (widescreen)
- `9:16`: Portrait (vertical, mobile-optimized)
- `1:1`: Square
- `4:3`: Standard landscape
- `3:4`: Standard portrait

resolution.description:
Output video resolution. It sets the price per second. The value is the
short side of the MP4; the long side follows the aspect ratio.
- `480P`: 480p SD (854x480 at 16:9)
- `720P`: 720p HD
- `1080P`: 1080p Full HD

duration.description: Duration of the output video in seconds. It sets the price together with `resolution`.

generate_audio.description: Whether to generate a synchronized audio track (dialogue, sound effects, music) with the video. It does not affect the price.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible generation. Fixing it improves reproducibility but does not guarantee identical results.

endpoints.summary: Voiceover - Generate speech from text
endpoints.description:
Generate natural-sounding speech from text using ElevenLabs AI voices.

Create professional voiceovers for videos, podcasts, presentations, and more.
Supports multiple languages, voice customization, and high-quality audio output.

text.description: The text to convert to speech. Supports UTF-8 characters including accented letters and non-Latin scripts.

voice_id.description: The unique identifier of the ElevenLabs voice to use for synthesis. You can find voice IDs in the ElevenLabs voice library.

stability.description: Controls voice consistency and expressiveness. Lower values (0.0) produce more expressive and varied speech, while higher values (1.0) produce more consistent and stable output.

similarity_boost.description: Controls how closely the generated voice matches the original voice sample. Higher values produce closer matching but may introduce artifacts.

speed.description: Speech rate multiplier. 0.7 is 30% slower than normal, 1.0 is normal speed, 1.2 is 20% faster.

use_speaker_boost.description: Enable speaker boost for enhanced voice clarity and presence in the generated audio.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

endpoints.summary: Voiceover - Generate speech with ElevenLabs v3
endpoints.description:
Generate expressive, natural-sounding speech from text with the ElevenLabs v3 model.

Direct the performance with inline audio tags in square brackets, such as `[excited]`,
`[whispers]`, `[laughs]` or `[pause 1s]`: the model performs them instead of reading them aloud.
Up to 5,000 characters per request.

**Credits:** charged per started block of 10 characters of `text`.

The request is processed asynchronously: the endpoint returns a `task_id`
immediately. Retrieve the result by polling
`GET /v1/ai/voiceover/elevenlabs-v3/{task-id}` or by providing an optional `webhook_url`.

text.description:
The text to convert to speech, up to 5,000 characters. Supports UTF-8 characters including accented letters and non-Latin scripts.

Inline audio tags in square brackets direct the performance instead of being read aloud, e.g. `[excited]`, `[whispers]`, `[laughs]` or `[pause 1s]`.

voice_id.description: The unique identifier of the ElevenLabs voice to use for synthesis. You can find voice IDs in the ElevenLabs voice library.

stability.description: Controls how closely the delivery sticks to the voice versus how freely it performs the text: 0.0 (Creative) is the most expressive and follows audio tags most strongly, 0.5 (Natural) is balanced, 1.0 (Robust) is the most consistent.

similarity_boost.description: Controls how closely the generated voice matches the original voice. Higher values produce closer matching.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.

stability.description: Controls voice consistency and expressiveness. Lower values produce more expressive, varied delivery; higher values produce more consistent, stable output.

similarity_boost.description: Controls how closely the generated voice matches the original voice. Higher values produce closer matching.

webhook_url.description: Optional callback URL that will receive asynchronous notifications whenever the task changes status. The payload sent to this URL is the same as the corresponding GET endpoint response, but without the data field.
